member.name: T:HumanGateway.Edge.Artifacts.FilesystemArtifactStore
member.summary: Local filesystem (LOCAL-EDGE-1.5, EDGE-FR-02, ARTF-FR-01): bytes are stored content-addressed, named by their SHA-256 hex digest and sharded into two-level subdirectories (<root>/<aa>/<bb>/<64-hex>). Equal content always lands on the same path, so duplicate uploads are deduplicated with no re-transfer, and the address is verified against the bytes as they are written (tamper/corruption detection, SP-06).
member.remarks: Writes are atomic and crash-safe: bytes are streamed to a temp file in the destination directory, hashed incrementally, flushed to disk, then renamed into place ( with overwrite: false). A partial write therefore never appears at a content-addressed path — a killed process leaves only an orphaned temp file, never a corrupt artifact. Concurrent saves of identical content race to the same path and collapse to a single file (the loser observes the winner's rename and reports dedup).

member.name: T:HumanGateway.Edge.Storage.SqliteConnectionFactory
member.summary: Builds and opens SQLite connections with the durability PRAGMAs required by EDGE-FR-07 / NF-04.
member.remarks:
journal_mode=WAL — write-ahead logging so committed writes survive power loss and readers never block a writer (persisted in the database file).
synchronous=NORMAL — the durability/performance sweet spot for WAL mode; a power loss may lose the most recent transaction only in the (unlikely) failure window, never a committed one that preceded a checkpoint. A default SQLite connection (synchronous=FULL + rollback journal) can corrupt or lose committed writes on power failure, so this is mandatory.
foreign_keys=ON — per-connection; enforces the schema's relational invariants.
busy_timeout — per-connection; concurrent local clients (EDGE-FR-06, NF-01) contend on locks with a bounded wait rather than failing immediately with SQLITE_BUSY.
journal_mode and synchronous are durable database settings; re-applying them on every open is idempotent and ensures the settings hold even when the file was created by a different process.

member.name: T:HumanGateway.Edge.Sync.SyncWorker
member.summary:
The Edge Gateway's background sync worker (EDGE-FR-05, product vision §6.2/§10): a hosted service that periodically performs outbound-only sync with the Cloud Relay (SP-01). It drives the sync-engineer's — the engine owns cursor/idempotency/ordering decisions, the worker only orchestrates transport and lifecycle:
Push — build the next batch from the durable outbox via the engine, send it through , and mark the covered entries sent only after the Relay acknowledges (write-then-ack, EDGE-FR-04).
Pull — request inbound batches, apply them idempotently via the engine, and enqueue the resulting delivery acknowledgements for the next push (SYNC-FR-05).
The worker's cursor state is durable (SYNC-FR-03): the Relay-issued push cursor, the gateway's own pull cursor, and the in-flight push batch identity are persisted through so a restart resumes from the last cursor (never full-state resync, NF-02) and a retried push reuses the same batchId + idempotencyKey (SYNC-FR-02, NF-05). Transient failures back off with capped, jittered exponential backoff (SYNC-FR-04); outbox entries are never dropped and are never marked FAILED merely for being offline — they are retained and retried (WAITING_FOR_SYNC is a valid state, never an error). Every create was committed to SQLite before this worker ever saw it, so a crash mid-cycle can never lose or duplicate a message (EDGE-FR-07).
